issues.title: BaseModel causes information loss with Generic classes
issues.body:
### Initial Checks

- [X] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

Inheriting from Pydantic's `BaseModel` in a class heirarchy seems to cause `__orig_bases__` to have the value that one would expect for `__orig_bases__` in a parent class.

### Example Code

```Python
from typing import *
from pydantic import BaseModel

class A(BaseModel):
    pass

class AA(A):
    pass

T = TypeVar('T', bound=A)

class Component:
    pass

class B(Component, Generic[T]):
    pass

class C(B[AA]):
    pass

c = C()
print(c.__orig_bases__) # (__main__.B[__main__.AA],)

class PydanticComponent(BaseModel):
    pass

class B(PydanticComponent, Generic[T]):
    pass

class C(B[AA]):
    pass

c = C()
print(c.__orig_bases__)
# pydantic 2: (<class '__main__.PydanticComponent'>, typing.Generic[~T])
# pydantic 1: (__main__.B[__main__.AA],)
```

comments.body:
Converting existing code from v1 to v2 I now encountered this same issue. 
In my case I use `__orig_bases__` from `__init_subclass__` method to modify the type of a field.

Here is a quickly simplified example of what I'm trying to do for more context, this is to work with a Mongodb document with strongly typed ids:
```python
PrimaryKeyType = TypeVar("PrimaryKeyType")

class MongoDocument(pydantic.BaseModel, Generic[PrimaryKeyType]):
    id: Optional[PrimaryKeyType] = pydantic.Field(default=None, alias="_id")

    def __init_subclass__(cls, **kwargs: Any):
        super().__init_subclass__(**kwargs)
        class_args = typing.get_args(cls.__orig_bases__[0])
        if cls.model_fields["id"].annotation == Optional[PrimaryKeyType]:
            cls.model_fields["id"].annotation = ObjectId

class UserId(ObjectId):
    pass

class UserDocument(MongoDocument[UserId]):
    pass

class AnotherDocumentWithDefaultIdType(MongoDocument):
    pass
```
With this setup we have the ability to override the type of ids used with the correct properties (such as the alias) as well as set a default if not provide (ObjectId).
In v1 we also use the function `populate_validators` after modifying the field list, i'm not yet sure how I will make that work in v2.

I understand that this is quite a special use case but any workaround to get the correct `__orig_bases__` value would be much appreciated.

**Edit**: since v2 now handles Generics out of the box I decided to give up on the idea of setting a default on our generic values (I suppose will have to wait for python 3.13: https://peps.python.org/pep-0696/ ). And one alternative for my case instead of using `__orig_bases__` from `__init_subclass__`, I've found that I can figure out the declared type from `__pydantic_init_subclass__`  and checking the annotation from `cls.model_fields` (it is not yet set when `__init_subclass__` is called.)

here is a simple metaclass wrapper around pydantic's ModelMetaclass. Unfortunately, I do not know the pydantic internals well enough to fully integrate it. But maybe, this is still useful for resolving the type information. One problem seems to be that `__class_getitem__` is not correctly implemented by pydantic. 

```python
import typing
from typing import Any, Generic, Type

import pydantic
import pydantic._internal._model_construction as pydantic_meta

GenericAlias = typing._GenericAlias


T = typing.TypeVar("T")


class GenericModelMetaclass(pydantic_meta.ModelMetaclass):
    """
    Preserve the generic information of a Pydantic model.
    """

    def __new__(
        mcs,
        name: str,
        bases: tuple,
        namespace: dict[str, Any],
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> Type:
        orig_bases = namespace.get("__orig_bases__", tuple())

        # Create the class using Pydantic's metaclass
        cls = super().__new__(mcs, name, bases, namespace, **kwargs)

        # Make the class behave like a GenericAlias when subscripted
        def __class_getitem__(cls, params):
            if not isinstance(params, tuple):
                params = (params,)

            # Create a new parameterized version
            param_type = GenericAlias(origin=cls, args=params)
            return param_type

        cls.__class_getitem__ = classmethod(__class_getitem__)
        # set the original bases
        cls.__orig_bases__ = orig_bases
        return cls


class PydanticBase(
    pydantic.BaseModel, typing.Generic[T], metaclass=GenericModelMetaclass
):
    x: T


class PydanticChild(PydanticBase[int]):
    pass


class Base(typing.Generic[T]):
    x: T


class Child(Base[int]):
    pass


objectT = typing.TypeVar("objectT", bound=object)


class PydanticObjectBase(PydanticBase[objectT], Generic[objectT, T]):
    x: objectT


class SomeClass:
    pass


class IndirectChild(PydanticObjectBase[SomeClass, SomeClass]):
    pass


def test():
    # __class_getitem__ is used to create a new parameterized version of the class
    assert Base[int] == Base.__class_getitem__(int)

    # it returns a GenericAlias
    assert isinstance(Base[int], GenericAlias)

    # a Child subclass of Base should have a __orig_bases__  with the original base class
    assert Child.__orig_bases__ == (Base[int],)

    base = Child.__orig_bases__[0]
    assert typing.get_origin(base) == Base
    assert typing.get_args(base) == (int,)

    pydantic_base = PydanticBase[int]

    assert typing.get_origin(pydantic_base) == PydanticBase
    assert typing.get_args(pydantic_base) == (int,)

    child = PydanticChild(x=1)
    assert child.__class__.__orig_bases__ == (PydanticBase[int],)

    indirect_child = IndirectChild(x=SomeClass())
    assert indirect_child.__class__.__orig_bases__ == (
```

We ended up writing a helper function that looks like this to get the original geneeric arg type as a real type at runtime instead of a string reference or python object `id`.
```python
def _extract_baseevent_result_type(cls: type) -> Any:
    """Extract T_EventResultType Generic arg from BaseEvent[T_EventResultType] subclasses using pydantic generic metadata."""
    
    # Look through MRO for a parameterized BaseEvent parent
    for parent in cls.__mro__:
        if hasattr(parent, '__pydantic_generic_metadata__'):
            metadata = getattr(parent, '__pydantic_generic_metadata__', {})
            # Check if this is a parameterized BaseEvent
            origin = metadata.get('origin')
            args = metadata.get('args')
            if origin is BaseEvent and args and len(args) > 0:
                result = args[0]
                return result
    
    return None

_extract_baseevent_result_type(BaseEvent[list[EmailMessage]])
# list[EmailMessage]
```

✅ Which allows me to do:
```python

ResultType = TypeAdapter(result_type)
cast_result = ResultType.validate_python(result_value)
```

issues.title: Constructor not called when `from_attributes=True` is used
issues.body:
### Initial Checks

- [X] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

Had some V1 code that I was porting to V2 and noticed a bug with PrivateAttrs set in the constructor of a model.  The constructor is not consistently called. Specifically if a random model is passed to `model_validate()` which can be parsed with `from_attributes`. See example for more details. I technically reference `self` in my real code which is why I had to do in in the constructor and not in a `default_factory`.


### Example Code

```Python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, PrivateAttr

class Foo:
    def __init__(self):
        self.foo = "baz"

class Example(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)
    foo: str = "bar"
    _priv: str = PrivateAttr()

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        print("here")
        self._priv = "password"

# e = Example() # This enters the constructor
# e = Example.model_validate({"foo": "bip"}) # This enters the constructor
e = Example.model_validate(Foo()) # This does not enter the constructor
```

comments.body:
@rafales  The reason its filed under a bug is because it breaks specifically how `PrivateAttr`s are supposed to work, without the constructor, you can't create a private attribute based on a users input.

SQLAlchemy does this a little different by using `__new__` when reading from a database  but also works a little different. When SQLAlchemy reads from a database, it expects the data to match the model and thus does not call the models initializer. I.e. it calls `__new__` but never calls `__init__`. For SQLAlchemy this makes a little sense though its worth noting they add `@reconstructor` to work around the fact that they do not call the initializer.

Pydantic is different, specifically with `model_validate`. I am asking Pydantic to create a model based on the object I pass it, I am not saying the object I pass it directly maps to the model, I just want pydantic to rip attributes from it. I.e. I am using `from_attributes`, not `from_identical_model`.

In theory, if the stance pydantic wants to take is the SQLAlchemy approach, they can change the docs to have people overwrite `__new__` instead of `__init__` for `PrivateAttr`s though I would argue this is still a bug and falls under a violation of the least surprise principal. If I call a function with three different arguments, I wouldn't expect 2 instances to call the initializer and one not to. If its a surprise, its a bug. No one likes to read docs that say "if you do ... than X BUT if you do ... then its Y or possible even Z if you do ...".

Pydantic is not an ORM, it should be calling the initializer (`__init__`).

issues.title: JSON schema of `bytes` ignores `val_json_bytes` in validation mode
issues.body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

The JSON schema of a `bytes` field takes its `format` from `ser_json_bytes` in both modes, but validation decodes input according to `val_json_bytes`. When only one of them is `'base64'`, the validation schema describes the wrong input: `binary` for a field that decodes base64 (below), or `base64url` for a field that keeps the string as is (`ser_json_bytes='base64'` alone).

I'd expect the validation schema to follow `val_json_bytes`, in line with #13711, which stopped applying `ser_json_temporal` to validation schemas. I have a small fix with a test and can open a PR.

### Example Code

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


class Model(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(val_json_bytes='base64')
```

Here is a minimal example, it does not work starting with depth equal to 256:
```python
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Optional
import json
from pydantic import BaseModel

class A(BaseModel):
    a: Optional[A]

n = 256
s = "{\"a\": " * n + "null" + "}" * n
A.model_validate(json.loads(s))
```

While searching for it, I also found the following snippet that hangs for no reason, with the depth starting at 128:
```python
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Literal, Annotated
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class EventSequence(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["Sequence"] = "Sequence"
    elements: list[Event]

class EventTactic(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["Tactic"] = "Tactic"
    details: Event

type Event = Annotated[EventSequence | EventTactic, Field(discriminator="type")]

def deep(n):
    return EventTactic(details=deep(n - 1)) if n > 0 else EventSequence(elements=[])

event = deep(128)
event.model_dump()
```

@Viicos confirmed this is still reproducing on the latest release: pydantic 2.14.1 / pydantic-core 2.50.1 (Oct 2026).

**Validation repro** (from @afdw above, depth 256, no actual cycle in the input):

```python
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Optional
import json
from pydantic import BaseModel

class A(BaseModel):
    a: Optional[A]

n = 256
s = "{\"a\": " * n + "null" + "}" * n
A.model_validate(json.loads(s))
```

Still raises:
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for A
a.a.a.a.a... (256 deep)
Recursion error - cyclic reference detected [type=recursion_loop]


**Serialization repro** (discriminated union, depth 128):

```python
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Literal, Annotated
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class EventSequence(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["Sequence"] = "Sequence"
    elements: list[Event]

class EventTactic(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["Tactic"] = "Tactic"
    details: Event

type Event = Annotated[EventSequence | EventTactic, Field(discriminator="type")]

def deep(n):
    return EventTactic(details=deep(n - 1)) if n > 0 else EventSequence(elements=[])

event = deep(128)
event.model_dump()
```

Behavior has changed since the last report. It no longer hangs, it now fails fast with:

ValueError: Circular reference detected (depth exceeded)


So there are two separate false positives here, one on validation (`recursion_loop`) and one on serialization (`Circular reference detected`), both triggered by deeply nested but fully acyclic structures. Neither input has a real cycle.

Given this reproduces cleanly on current main, is this still expected to need a smaller minimal case, or is the one above enough to act on?
